commands.name: traits
commands.description: Show jev-traits status, or check changes against the repository traits
commands.output:
jev-traits · jev-latest · fix ≥ 0.8 · double-check ≥ 0.5 · pass ≥ 0.9 · edits checked
jev-traits found no TypeSafe API key. Store it once, by hand, in the macOS Keychain (jev-lint reads the same item):

  security add-generic-password -U -a "$USER" -s typesafe-api-key -w

The command prompts for the key, so it stays out of your shell history and this chat. Then run /traits again.
Lookup order: the typesafe_api_key option (kept in secure storage, once the plugin is installed from a marketplace),
then the Keychain item typesafe-api-key, then TYPESAFE_API_KEY as a fallback for machines without the item, such as CI.
Do not keep the key in a .env file.
Traits: no .agents/traits folder at or above /work/app. Add one as .agents/traits/<name>.md.
Run /traits check [changed|staged|unstaged|untracked|<files…>] to check work in progress.

tools.name: check_traits
tools.description: Checks code against this repository's traits (.agents/traits/*.md and .agents/traits/<group>/*.md) with the traits CLI and TypeSafe Jev. Use it before committing (target staged), after adding or revising a trait, or to audit files. Findings are fast model judgments: read the trait and the code before changing anything, and report unsure results as unsure, never as passes.

script: tool.call Bash rm -rf build && git push --force origin main
